The Mn concentration in the (Ga,Mn)N films was tuned from 0.2% to 10% by varying the growth temperature from 700°C to 590°C.
The (Ga,Mn)N films exhibited ferromagnetic behavior with Curie temperatures ranging from 3 to 10 K for Mn concentrations above 5%.
Synchrotron-based XANES and DFT modeling indicated that the Mn ions predominantly exist in the +3 charge state in the GaN host.
TEM analysis confirmed the uniform distribution of Mn in the GaN lattice, with no evidence of phase separation, clusters, or nanocrystals.
Even a 10°C variation in local substrate temperature could lead to a 40% dispersion in the Curie temperature of the (Ga,Mn)N films.
The growth rate of the (Ga,Mn)N films ranged from 20 to 50 nm/h, depending on the growth temperature.
The root-mean-square surface roughness of the films remained below 3.5 nm, even for the film grown at the lowest temperature of 590°C.
The authors emphasize the importance of accounting for local temperature variations across the substrate during the growth of ternary or more complex semiconductor compounds.

Ferromagnetic (Ga,Mn)N has potential technological relevance for device applications, such as dissipation-less information transfer and the manipulation of magnetic anisotropy through electric-field-generated strain.
The authors used a range of characterization techniques, including AFM, SIMS, TEM, and XRD, to probe the structural and compositional properties of the (Ga,Mn)N films.
The authors found that the Mn incorporation and Curie temperature of the (Ga,Mn)N films were strongly correlated with the local substrate temperature.
The authors grew the (Ga,Mn)N films on commercially available GaN(0001) templates deposited on c-oriented sapphire substrates.
The (Ga,Mn)N films were grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy under nominally nitrogen-rich conditions.
The authors used a Ti backside metallization to improve the radiative heat exchange and ensure effective temperature control during the growth.
The authors performed detailed temperature mapping across the substrate to investigate the impact of local temperature variations on the magnetic properties of the (Ga,Mn)N films.
